Stage 3 · Grammar

The passive

When it does not matter who did it — or nobody knows.

Read these four sentences from the recording you are about to hear.
  • Metal containers were invented in 1810.
  • Those first cans were made of iron.
  • Over 18 billion cans are produced every year in the UK.
  • The safe modern tin opener wasn’t invented until 1925.
In these four sentences, what is missing that a normal sentence has?
The same event, two ways
 PresentPast
ActiveMachines produce the cans.Appert invented the can.
PassiveThe cans are produced by machines.The can was invented by Appert.
NegativeThe cans are not produced here.It was not invented until 1925.
QuestionAre they produced here?When was it invented?
The formulabe (am / is / are / was / were) + past participle — made, produced, invented, sold, eaten, thrown
After the verb recycledA preposition still forces -ing: The noodles are boiled before serving.
Now write the past participle of each verb.
1produce →
2make →
3eat →
4throw →
5sell →
6grow →
7freeze →

FORM. be + past participle. The tense lives in be: is made / was made.

USE. Use it when the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant. Add by… only when the doer is genuinely interesting: invented by a French chef.

Not “It was invent in 1810”, not “The cans are make by machine”, not “It is happened” — happen has no passive.

The passive comes back next lesson inside a restaurant review: the fish was overcooked.

FORM. be + past participle. Everything the tense has to say is said by be: is / are made for the present, was / were made for the past. The participle itself never changes.

USE 1 — the doer is unknown. The tin opener was not invented until 1925. Nobody in the sentence needs to know who did not invent it.

USE 2 — the doer is obvious or unimportant. Cans are produced by machine. Milk is sold in cartons. We care about the thing, not the worker.

USE 3 — you want the thing at the front. A sentence starts with what it is about. If the topic is the can, the can goes first, and the passive is the only way to do that.

WHEN TO ADD BY. Only when the doer is news: invented by a French chef called Monsieur Appert. In most passive sentences there is no by at all, and adding one sounds heavy.

The three mistakes to watch: “It was invent” (no participle) · “The cans are make by machine” (base form instead of the participle) · “The accident was happened” (verbs with no object — happen, arrive, go, come — have no passive at all).

Next lesson you will use the passive to complain and to write a review: my fish was overcooked, we were charged for two coffees.

Five real passive sentences from Audio 10.4. Press Listen on each one.

Full grammar reference — The passive: Present Simple and Past Simple

Form

Present passiveCheese is made from milk. · The cans are transported by lorry.
Past passiveThe tin was invented in 1810. · The tomatoes were grown in Spain.
NegativeIt isn’t sold here. · They weren’t picked by hand.
QuestionIs it made in Kazakhstan? · When was it invented?
Saying who did it… by a small company in Almaty.

Spelling and sound

The passive always uses the past participle: make → made, grow → grown, invent → invented, write → written.

When and why we use it

  • Use the passive when the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant, and the thing itself is the point.
  • It is the normal voice for processes, instructions and history: The fruit is washed, then it is cut, then it is packed.
  • Add by + the doer only if that information matters.
  • The tense is shown by be: is made (present), was made (past).

Signal words

is / are + participle · was / were + participle · by · then · after that · finally

Watch out — the mistakes learners really make

  • Cheese is make from milk. → Cheese is made from milk.Participle, not the plain verb.
  • The tin invented in 1810. → The tin was invented in 1810.be is missing.
  • The soup was cooked by slowly. → The soup was cooked slowly.By introduces a person, not a manner.
  • It is used to make bread by bakers every day. → Bakers use it to make bread.If the doer matters, the active is clearer.

Don’t confuse it with

Active: Somebody serves the soup cold. Passive: The soup is served cold. Same event, different focus.
